renumber_note: Registration v3, revised BEFORE the full run. v2 removed edge-clipped objects (smoke: the left bowling pin sits at the left edge; its right-view copy is out of frame at ~364 px disparity). v3 additionally moves cross-view correspondence from the VLM to the geometry module: NCC template matching guided by the left bbox. Smoke showed the VLM's independent bbox localization in the two views has ~50+ px noise and near-identical y bounds -- its noise swamps the ~130 px disparity signal, so cross-view correspondence is precisely the kind of mechanical work the spatial-language architecture assigns to geometry. GT: dmin NOT added to the depth formula (disp1.png values ARE the view1<->view5 pixel offsets in shipped coordinates; verified by NCC template matching at 150 px measured vs 154 px map, 3%).
name: Real-world stereo OOD: spatial language pipeline on Middlebury 2006
registered_before_run: 2026-10-11 (before any model call on these images)
question: Does the P275/P276 architecture conclusion (geometry module emits numbers, recognition outsourced to a detector, LLM never produces coordinates) survive contact with REAL stereo images, where texture and lighting are uncontrolled?

data.pairs: view1/view5 at Illum2/Exp1, rectified, radial distortion removed
data.calibration: f = 3740 px at original resolution (3072 px wide) scaled to full-size by f_full = 3740 * W_full / 3072; baseline B = 160 mm between views 1 and 5; dmin.txt added to disparity maps
data.ground_truth: GT disparity maps disp1.png sampled at the left bbox center (41 px window, nonzero median, plus dmin); Z_gt = f_full * B / disp_gt
data.metric_note: Scores use RELATIVE depth error |Z_est-Z_gt|/Z_gt, which is invariant to the f_full scaling ambiguity (original-resolution assumption 3072 px).

arms.SL: VLM localizes the object in the LEFT view only (bbox, coarse) -> geometry module runs NCC template matching in the right view (mechanical correspondence, sub-noise of any model) -> disparity d -> Z = f_full * B / d. No depth number and no cross-view correspondence ever comes from a model.
arms.Direct: VLM sees the LEFT image only and directly estimates the object distance in meters. Current-default way.

predictions.claim: SL median relative depth error < 15% AND significantly smaller than Direct (one-sided sign-flip permutation p < 0.05).
predictions.falsifies: If Direct <= SL or SL median >= 15%, the mechanical stereo layer does not carry to real images.

predictions.claim: Direct (single-view) depth estimates show a systematic signed bias (median signed error away from zero) — the VLM has no metric depth scale from one image.
predictions.falsifies: If Direct signed errors are centered on zero with small spread, single-view depth guessing is better than claimed.

predictions.claim: Every SL failure is attributable to a mechanical stage (bbox parse failure, edge clipping, low NCC < 0.3, degenerate disparity) while Direct failures/errors are not attributable.
predictions.falsifies: If SL fails opaquely, grounding does not transfer to the real pipeline.

fairness_notes: Object list frozen above before any model call; the VLM is never shown the disparity maps or calibration.
Direct gets the same image resolution as SL's left view.

GT sampling uses the SL left bbox location - declared; a wrong-object bbox poisons GT too and falls into wrong_object attribution, which is conservative AGAINST SL only if the same wrong bbox also drives its own disparity... declared limitation.
Both arms use the same VLM (doubao-seed-2.1-lite vision).
